description: Prep-state-sensitive decomposer scenarios. Each scenario is a free-text dish + the prep-state assertions a curator would make on the resolved CNF ingredients. The probe walks recipe.ingredients, finds the first ingredient whose food_description contains the keyword (case-insensitive), and scores its extracted prep state against the assertion. Pattern mirrors backend/_decomposer_lab_scenarios.json but the metric is prep-state correctness, not energy density.

schema.dish: free-text dish name fed to decomposer.decompose()
schema.rationale: why this check matters — feeds the report

scenarios.rationale: Soup means cooked. Picking raw carrot here would underestimate Na (carrot raw 69 mg vs boiled+salt 302 mg per 100 g).
Explicit 'raw' in dish name. Should pick FoodID 2380.
Fried plantain side — must resolve to cooked plantain (FoodID 1662), not raw 1661. Vit C raw 18.4 mg vs cooked 10.9 mg per 100 g; fat raw 0.37 g vs cooked 0.18 g.
Porridge means cooked. WAFCT plantain porridge is a primary West African meal.

scenarios.dish: scrambled eggs and white toast breakfast
scenarios.rationale: Egg in scrambled context — must be cooked (FoodID 133 scrambled or any cooked variant). Picking raw egg 125 is a contamination error.
Grilled / roasted / cooked chicken — raw chicken 560 is wrong by ~30 kcal/100 g and clinically wrong (food safety).

scenarios.dish: fresh apple slices with peanut butter
scenarios.rationale: Snack context — raw apple (1696). Picking baked/canned/dried apple would change sugar profile.
Pie filling is cooked — could be canned-heated (1487), boiled (1698), or microwaved (1486). All acceptable.

scenarios.dish: canned tomato pasta sauce over spaghetti
scenarios.rationale: Sauce is canned. Picking fresh tomato underestimates Na (canned tomato has added salt).
Garden salad — all components raw. Picking cooked greens would wreck Vit C.
Stew means cooked beef. Raw beef is a food-safety error.
Frozen broccoli used in stir-fry — should resolve to FoodID 2026 (frozen+boiled) not 2025 (frozen unprep).

scenarios.dish: bowl of corn flakes with cold milk
scenarios.rationale: Packaged RTE cereal + pasteurized milk. Decomposer should NOT add a cooking verb; both components are eaten as-is.
Heated frozen entree → cooked thermal, frozen preservation. Decomposer should pick a frozen-entree CNF row, not a fresh-prepared lasagna recipe.

scenarios.dish: ramen instant noodle cup, dry pack
scenarios.rationale: Instant noodles are precooked-then-dried (preservation=dried per Phase 1.6 extractor). Picking a fresh-cooked noodle row would inflate water content.

scenarios.dish: canned tuna salad sandwich on white bread
scenarios.rationale: Canned tuna + commercial bread. Canned tuna ≠ fresh tuna (different Na, different oil content).

scenarios.dish: instant oatmeal packet, prepared with hot water
scenarios.rationale: Instant oatmeal: dehydrated oats reconstituted with water → end state is cooked. Decomposer should pick a cooked-oatmeal row, not raw oats.

scenarios.dish: fruit-flavored yogurt cup with granola topping
scenarios.rationale: Fermented dairy + RTE granola. Phase 1.6 extractor maps yogurt→fermented. Granola is RTE.
